scenario: In the real dataset (parsed from each book's HTML, header and footer already removed), wrapped lines inside a paragraph are separated by CRLF CRLF and paragraphs by three CRLFs (Alice: 1721 double, 821 triple, 2 lone newlines; early etexts use LF LF for wraps). _PARAGRAPH_BREAK splits on every wrapped line, strip_gutenberg_boilerplate rejoins with a blank line, erasing the wrap-vs-paragraph difference, so _unwrap never sees a multi-line paragraph and chunk_passages packs one-line pieces separated by blank lines. On real Alice: 67 passages averaging 37 blank lines each, e.g. 'Suddenly she came upon a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass;' / blank / 'there was nothing on it except a tiny golden key...'; 1322 of 2476 blank-line breaks fall between a line with no end mark and a lowercase continuation. The whole books dataset (15M tokens) would teach the model a blank line every ~12 words, which R1 forbids fixing in output, so players would see it. Nothing fails, so it is silent. Tests pass because the fixture uses classic PG plain-text layout (header, single-newline wraps), which the real source never contains.
title: Real sedthh/gutenberg_english TEXT puts a blank line after every wrapped line, so every books passage has blank lines mid-sentence and real paragraph breaks are lost

evidence: p1_basic.py and p8_simp.py use the real load path (row_has_format, row_to_content, prepare_content) and textproc.simplicity; doubling the vocab from 1,465 to 2,931 words raised the FineWeb median from 0.515 to 0.596. fix: Re-derive the thresholds from the real simple_vocab before the full build, e.g. measure the simplicity distribution of the first few thousand rows per source and set simplicity_min at a chosen keep-quantile (simplest half: about 0.6-0.65 for FineWeb), or express simplicity_min as a quantile. Record the target keep-rate in the Task 15 notes, check build time (more rows streamed), and consider extending the filter to cosmo_openstax (median 0.47) as the Task 14 ruling anticipated.
scenario: Spec §4 says text is selected for short sentences and common vocabulary so 1-40M models can learn it. Real rows scored with the real simplicity() against a simple_vocab built from 400 real TinyStories rows (2,931 words, smaller than the build's 6,000, so these are lower bounds): FineWeb 96.8% pass (median 0.59), FineWeb-Edu 96.0% (median 0.55), Simple Wikipedia 99.3% (median 0.66). The median web sentence is 16.5 words, below the 18-word knee, so the sentence-length factor almost never binds; only about 3% of docs (technical pages with 30-44-word sentences) are rejected. The web dataset (30M tokens) and the fineweb_edu and simplewiki shares (about 11M) enter at full FineWeb complexity, and changing this later needs another full build.
title: Simplicity thresholds (0.35 web/edu, 0.30 Simple Wikipedia) keep about 97-100% of real documents, so the spec's simplicity filtering does nothing for 30-40% of the corpus
